manifest.name: @lone-wolf-akela/dsh-sandboxie-redirect
manifest.description: DSH bundle adding a copy-on-write permission preset: shell commands run inside a per-workspace Sandboxie box, so writes outside the workspace land in the box's copy while the real disk is untouched.
manifest.author: lone-wolf-akela

scripts.test: node test/unit.mjs && node test/sbie-locate.mjs && node test/dsh-locate.mjs && node test/tool-execute.mjs && node test/host-projection.mjs && node test/validate-patch.mjs

bundle.text:
# dsh-sandboxie-redirect — the bundle layer.
#
# `dsh plugin --profile <name> add @lone-wolf-akela/dsh-sandboxie-redirect` appends this package
# to the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles`; the next profile boot applies THIS
# layer. Rows reference the package by NAME, not by path: Node resolution finds
# the installed code through the profile's package graph, so the same file works
# from npm, a tarball, a `link:` checkout or `github:` install.
#
# Two consequences of the patch vocabulary, both load-bearing:
#
#   * On a NON-insert patch, `name` is a GUARD rather than a reassignment:
#     applyEntryPatches keeps `id` plus the remaining overrides and skips the
#     whole patch when `name` does not equal the target row's name. The stock
#     provider row therefore cannot be re-pointed in place — it is DISABLED
#     here, and ours is inserted as its own row.
#
#   * A patch replaces a row's entire `config` (no deep merge). Restating the
#     stock presets as literals would therefore silently DISCARD any preset a
#     later DSH version or another bundle contributes. So `presets` is computed:
#     it reads whatever the layers before this one composed and merges ours in,
#     falling back to the literal stock three when that composition cannot be
#     read. The failure mode is the old behaviour — never a preset directory
#     that is missing the shipped presets.
#
# The plugin's own README documents what the preset does; the reasoning behind
# this file's shape lives in AGENTS.md.

# The stock shell-sandbox provider is replaced by ours. `runnerCommand` cannot
# do this job: a configured runner applies to EVERY mode, whereas only the
# copy-on-write *preset* should be diverted.
- id: sandbox
  name: "@deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox-local"
  disabled: true

- id: permission
  name: "@deepseek-ai/dsh-permission-presets"
  config:
    # The leading glyph in the display name is deliberate and load-bearing: the
    # shipped dropdown takes its icons from a CLOSED id->icon map, so a custom
    # preset renders with none, and the label span is not a stable handle for a
    # DOM shim (its shape changes when the row is selected). The name is host
    # config rendered verbatim in every surface, so the glyph belongs here.
    # The preset also deliberately bundles the LEGAL `workspace-write` mode: the
    # preset identity is what selects the redirect, so the session projection
    # schema, SANDBOX_MODES, the file fence and the escalation tables all stay
    # untouched.
    presets: !!js >-
      (() => {
      const copyOnWrite = {
      sandbox: "workspace-write",
      approval: "ask",
      name: "❐ Copy-on-write 写时复制",
      description: "Writes inside the workspace go to the real disk; writes, edits and deletes anywhere else still succeed but land in this workspace's Sandboxie copy, which SandMan can inspect, recover or discard. 工作区内的写入照旧落到真实磁盘；工作区外的写入、修改、删除不会失败，改落到本工作区的 Sandboxie 副本里。"
      };
      const stock = {
      "read-only": { sandbox: "read-only", approval: "ask" },
      "workspace-write": { sandbox: "workspace-write", approval: "ask" },
      "danger-full-access": { sandbox: "danger-full-access", approval: "never" }
      };
      let base;
      try {
      base = [...ctx.loader.entries()].find((entry) => entry.options?.id === "permission")?.options?.config?.presets;
      } catch {}
      const usable = base !== undefined && base !== null && ["read-only", "workspace-write", "danger-full-access"].every((key) => base[key] !== undefined);
      const source = usable ? base : stock;
      const keys = Object.keys(source).filter((key) => key !== "copy-on-write");
      const after = keys.indexOf("workspace-write");
      keys.splice(after === -1 ? keys.length : after + 1, 0, "copy-on-write");
      return Object.fromEntries(keys.map((key) => [key, key === "copy-on-write" ? copyOnWrite : source[key]]));
      })()

# ONE row into this package, and that is a hard requirement: the client-modules
# registry composes a `dsh.client` package only while exactly ONE of its loader
# entries is active, and it fails the whole boot otherwise. The header chip, the
# policy note and the `sandbox_clear` tool are plain imports wired from this
# row's constructor (see wireCompanions() in lib/provider.mjs).
- insert:
    - id: sandbox-copy-on-write
      name: "@lone-wolf-akela/dsh-sandboxie-redirect"

readme.text:
[](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@lone-wolf-akela/dsh-sandboxie-redirect)
[](https://github.com/lone-wolf-akela/dsh-sandboxie-redirect/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[](LICENSE)
[](#installation)

> **中文版**：[README.zh.md](README.zh.md)

A [DSH](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) bundle that adds a fourth permission preset, **Copy-on-write (写时复制)**: shell commands run inside a Sandboxie box dedicated to the workspace, so writes inside the workspace land on the real disk as usual, while writes, edits and deletions anywhere else keep succeeding — but only inside that box's copy. The three shipped presets (read-only, workspace-write, danger-full-access) behave exactly as before.

```
┌─ your DSH session ────────────────┐
│  file policy: copy-on-write       │
│                                   │
│  shell command ──▶ Sandboxie box ─┼──▶ workspace writes    → real disk

- Windows only, and it needs [Sandboxie-Plus](https://sandboxie-plus.com/) installed (the sandbox service must be running).
- It is a permission **preset**, not a patch to the DSH application: nothing inside the app is modified.
- Its purpose is accident prevention, undo, and keeping system directories clean. It is **not** a defence against malicious programs — Sandboxie itself makes no such promise, and a plugin runs with the same access as the app hosting it.

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Real disk | Where files actually live (for example `C:\Users\…`). |
| Sandbox / box | The isolated environment Sandboxie creates. This plugin creates one per workspace. |
| Copy | The box's private storage for changes to files outside the workspace (under the sandbox root), kept apart from the real files. |
| Inside / outside the box | Under Copy-on-write, shell commands run inside the box; the DSH app and its file tools (read/write/edit) run outside it. |
| Merged view | What a command inside the box sees: the copy's content overlaid on the real file. |
| SandMan | Sandboxie-Plus's GUI, for inspecting, recovering and deleting sandboxes. |

**Prerequisite:** [Sandboxie-Plus](https://sandboxie-plus.com/) ([source](https://github.com/sandboxie-plus/Sandboxie)). The installer must have created its service; every box this plugin uses is created and managed by Sandboxie.

**Any installation folder works — there is nothing to configure.** The plugin does not assume Sandboxie lives in one fixed directory: it reads Sandboxie's own registry entries first (the `SbieSvc` service's `ImagePath` is the authority — an installation that can create a box always has it, followed by the driver service and the installer's uninstall entry), then the conventional folders and `PATH`, and only as a last resort sweeps well-known parent folders and each fixed drive's root for a folder named after Sandboxie that holds `SbieDll.dll`. Another drive, a per-user folder and a portable directory all work. Only when every one of those comes up empty does it report "not installed", and that message names `DSH_SBIE_DIR` (see [Environment](#environment)) as the way to point at it directly.

**DSH's own installation folder is not assumed either.** The `koffi.node` the launcher needs ships *inside* DSH, under its `resources\app.asar.unpacked`, and the launcher is a plain Node process with no `process.resourcesPath`. So the plugin locates DSH itself: the Node running the launcher (the desktop app's own runtime lives inside the installation, so that path points back at it), then the installer's uninstall entry, then the conventional folders and `PATH`. DSH installed on another drive works too.

The package is a DSH *bundle*: installing it also adds its configuration layer, so no profile file needs hand-editing.

```powershell

readme.section: install into a profile (the CLI creates it if needed and appends this bundle)
readme.text: dsh plugin --profile <profile> add @lone-wolf-akela/dsh-sandboxie-redirect

readme.section: check the layer without booting, then start
readme.text:
dsh --profile <profile> --dump-config      # expect a "# == @lone-wolf-akela/dsh-sandboxie-redirect" layer
dsh --profile <profile>
```

Other supported sources, for a local checkout or an offline machine:

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add C:\path\to\dsh-sandboxie-redirect   # a checkout (linked)
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add .\lone-wolf-akela-dsh-sandboxie-redirect-0.3.1.tgz
```

readme.section: check the layer without booting, then start
readme.text: > **Which command for which profile?** The CLI refuses to touch a profile that a running desktop app owns (`profile "desktop" is managed exclusively by the Electron application`). For that profile, install from inside the app: **Settings → Plugins → add a bundle**, and give the package name above. For any other profile, the CLI works normally.

readme.section: check the layer without booting, then start
readme.text: Then restart the client, open the permission dropdown, and select **❐ Copy-on-write 写时复制**. The preset appears once per session as needed; the title bar shows the box name after the first shell command.

Earlier revisions were installed by copying the tree into `~/.dsh/plugins/dsh-sandboxie-redirect` and adding rows to `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml`. If your profile still carries those rows, **remove them** before switching to the bundle channel: two active rows into the same `dsh.client` package fail the boot ("resolves from multiple active Loader sources"). The rows to delete are the ones whose `name` is an absolute path ending in `lib\provider.mjs`, plus the `sandbox` and `permission` rows this plugin added. `tools/install.mjs` remains in the repository for that manual channel, and it must be run outside the sandbox.

| Location | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Writes, edits, deletions **inside** the workspace | Applied directly to the real disk |
| Writes, edits **outside** the workspace | The command reports success, but the change lands in that workspace's box copy; the real disk is untouched |
| Deletions **outside** the workspace | The real file survives; the copy records only a deletion marker |

DSH's own file tools (read/write/edit) run outside the box and keep the workspace-write rule: writable inside the workspace, refused outside it. To read a file *as the sandbox sees it*, read it with a shell command — see [Read-side divergence](#read-side-divergence).

Under this preset the session's policy text gains a paragraph that tells the model how the mode behaves and what to watch for, so an agent does not have to infer it.

readme.section: Sandbox name in the title bar
readme.text: Under Copy-on-write the title bar shows the box name (for example `dsh_able_willow`; hover for the copy's root). It appears only when both hold: this session's preset is Copy-on-write, and this workspace really owns a box — so it shows up after the first command, and disappears when the preset changes or the box is cleaned.

The preset carries an icon (two overlapping sheets) in the dropdown and the bottom button, following the active theme. The preset's display name starts with `❐` for the same reason: the shipped dropdown takes icons from a closed id→icon map, so the name is the one surface that always renders.

In-session, `sandbox_clear` inspects or discards this workspace's copy: `mode: "inspect"` reports (file count, size), `mode: "clear"` deletes the copy and its configuration. It works in every permission mode, and can only ever touch boxes Sandboxie attributes to *this* workspace. A diagnostic `mode: "status"` reports what the session projection registry holds for the calling session — it separates "the fold never ran" from "the client never got it", so it is the first thing to look at when the title-bar box name is missing (it only actually worked from 0.3.3 on).

- **The `sandbox_permissions` parameter description is not written for this preset.** DSH generates that one text for every preset, and it reads as "the retry after a denial" — under Copy-on-write an out-of-workspace write is never denied (it succeeds into the copy), so no denial marker appears and there is nothing to retry. The session's policy text says so explicitly; escalation is a deliberate "run this one call on the real disk" lever, not a follow-up to a failure.
- **Read-side divergence (important)**: one path can look different depending on who reads it.
  - Shell commands run inside the box and may see the merged view — if an earlier command wrote that file outside the workspace, the command sees the copy's version.
  - DSH's file tools run outside the box and always see the real disk.
  - So: to see "what a command wrote outside the workspace", read with a shell command; to see "was the real disk changed", read with DSH's file tools (or File Explorer).
- **Copy location**: ordinary paths at `<sandbox root>\drive\<drive>\<path>`; paths under the user profile at `<sandbox root>\user\current\<relative path>`. Sandboxie's own sandbox folder is followed automatically (its `Fil

```powershell
node bin\dsh-sbie-run.mjs --manage list                  # list managed boxes
node bin\dsh-sbie-run.mjs --manage clean "<workspace>"    # clean one workspace's boxes
node bin\dsh-sbie-run.mjs --manage delete-box <box>      # delete one box
```

`--manage` must run outside the box (an ordinary terminal, or a `danger-full-access` session): a process inside a box cannot see Sandboxie's box list. The same operations are available in SandMan.
All optional; each exists as an escape hatch rather than a configuration surface.

| Variable | Effect |
|---|---|
| `DSH_SBIE_DIR` | The Sandboxie installation folder (the one holding `SbieDll.dll`). Normally unnecessary: the automatic lookup reads Sandboxie's registry entries, the conventional folders and `PATH` first. Use it when Sandboxie lives somewhere unusual and that lookup misses it. |
| `DSH_SBIE_NODE` | The `node.exe` that runs the launcher. Set it if the plugin cannot find one (the desktop app's own runtime, then `$DSH_HOME/dsh-runtimes`, are searched automatically). |
| `DSH_SBIE_ROOT` | Overrides the sandbox root. Normally unnecessary: Sandboxie's configured `FileRootPath` is followed. Default `%SystemDrive%\Sandbox\%USERNAME%`. |
| `DSH_SBIE_LOG_DIR` | Where diagnostics land. Default `$DSH_HOME/state/dsh-sandboxie-redirect`. |
| `DSH_SBIE_INI` | The Sandboxie configuration file to read. Default `%SystemDrive%\Windows\Sandboxie.ini`. |
| `DSH_SBIE_KOFFI` / `DSH_SBIE_KOFFI_ROOT` | A `koffi.node` (or a directory holding one) for the launcher. Normally unnecessary: DSH's own installation folder is located automatically (see [Installation](#installation)). |
| `DSH_SBIE_BOX` / `DSH_SANDBOX_ROOT` | **Set by the plugin** inside a command; authoritative fo
Diagnostics: `provider.log`, `host.log`, `tool.log` under the log directory above. The host log is capped at 512 KB and records only state transitions.

- The bundle layer disables the stock `sandbox` row (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox-local`) and inserts this package's provider, which subclasses it: only the Copy-on-write *preset* is diverted, every other mode delegates to the stock ACL path. A configured `runnerCommand` cannot do this — it would apply to every mode.
- The same layer merges `copy-on-write` into the `permission` preset list, keeping whatever the layers before it contributed.
- Shell commands are then run through `bin/dsh-sbie-run.mjs`, a plain-Node child process that holds the Sandboxie FFI. Sandboxie builds processes through its service and drops the standard handles, so stdio is relayed over a loopback TCP channel with length-prefixed frames.
- Box names are a deterministic word pair derived from the workspace path (`dsh_<adjective>_<noun>`), so no state file is needed to find a workspace's box; a collision steps to the next candidate, and a name is only adopted when Sandboxie's own configuration says that workspace owns it.
- Only a failure to load the harness packages is fatal, and that case registers a provider that fails **closed** — refusing to run commands rather than running them unconfined.

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for setup and the development loop, and [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) for the architecture and the hard-won constraints. The short version:

```powershell
npm test                         # unit + host projection + bundle-layer validation (no DSH, no Sandboxie)
npm run test:acceptance          # acceptance: real boxes, real redirection (outside any box, medium IL)
npm run pack:check               # what the published tarball would contain
```
Security issues: see [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).
